title: re-embed-record.v1
description: A record of rebuilding one embedding store with a different model. It links the source and target embedding-portability.v1 documents by digest, declares the target model identity, and accounts for what was rebuilt, what it cost in batches, what left the machine, and what a quality comparison found. A quality block is evidence that a stated comparison ran and what it returned, never evidence that retrieval is good.

source_store.description: The embedding-portability.v1 store that supplied the retained source text.

target_store.description: The embedding-portability.v1 store this run produced.

quality.description: Absent when no comparison was attempted. Present with a status saying what the comparison found.

store_evidence_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the embedding-portability.v1 document bytes. The identifier selects the claim; this digest binds it to content.

model_identity.description: Model identity is the triple id + revision + dimensions. The same scheme at two dimensions is two models. Availability, any weights digest and any license are operator declarations the scanner cannot re-run.

batch_log.description: Accounting for a resumable run. The batch size is bounded so a run stays within memory regardless of store size.

resumed.description: True when this run continued an interrupted one from a checkpoint.

checkpoint_sha256.description: Digest of the final checkpoint file, when one was retained.

coverage.description: Only retained records are rebuilt. The four counts plus the failure count must equal total_records.

deleted_by_policy_skipped.description: Excluded by policy before any batch was formed, and never sent to a model.

egress.description: What left the machine. Local and offline is the default; a remote provider requires an explicit opt-in and is reported here.

status.description: sampled: thresholds met. below_threshold: the comparison ran and at least one threshold was not met. not_measured: no query set, or too small for sufficient evidence.

mode.description: record_anchored: a retained record's own stored vector is the query in each store, so neither model is needed at query time. text: free-text queries embedded by each store's own model, which only a reproducible built-in scheme can do offline.

metric_basis.description: What the metrics are about. neighborhood_agreement: whether the two stores place the same records near each other. retrieval_relevance: whether what was retrieved answers the query. record_anchored mode is always neighborhood_agreement, which is not a measurement of user search quality.

anchor_selection.description: How the query set was chosen. seeded_random: drawn by seeded hash over the record identifiers, so another party draws the same set. operator: supplied by the operator, who could have chosen the queries that flatter the result. An operator-chosen set reports normally but can never move a lock-in score.

anchor_seed.description: The seed the draw used, so the set can be redrawn. Required when anchor_selection is seeded_random and meaningless otherwise.

similarity.description: The similarity function the ranking used.

thresholds.description: The thresholds this run was judged against, by check name. Operator-declared, so they are attested and never verified: a passing run met the bar its operator set, which may be any bar at all. A reader must be shown these beside the label.

candidate_pool_size.description: How many records each query was ranked against. Smaller than the store when the pool was drawn, by the same seed, to keep the comparison bounded. A top_k_overlap is a share of this pool, not of the store.

tie_break.description: How equal similarities were ordered, so a reader can tell a tie from a disagreement.

boundary_ties.description: Queries whose top-k boundary fell inside a run of equal similarities, where membership was settled by the tie break rather than by the vectors.

queries_skipped.description: Queries that were declared but could not be evaluated, for example an anchor missing from one of the two stores.

correlation_undefined.description: True when rank correlation had no defined value for at least one query, for example because every candidate tied.

top_k_capped.description: True when a store held fewer records than the requested top_k, so the effective k was smaller.

metrics.description: Agreement metrics need no expected answers. Hit rate and MRR speak to correctness and are present only when the query set supplied expected records.
